description: The whole of what the webview may ask the Rust shell to do: THIRTY-FIVE entries, and nothing else. Two are core event permissions — `core:event:allow-listen` and `core:event:allow-unlisten`, which are exactly what `@tauri-apps/api/event`'s `listen()` and the unlisten function it returns invoke (`plugin:event|listen` / `plugin:event|unlisten`); the webview imports nothing else from Tauri but `invoke`, which needs no core grant for this app's own commands. `core:default` is deliberately NOT granted: it would hand the webview the live tray, menu and resources surfaces (`plugin:tray|new`, `plugin:menu|set_as_app_menu`, `plugin:resources|close`, …) and `plugin:event|emit`, which lets a webview forge a `state:changed` that Rust-side listeners receive. Thirty-two are this app's own commands: the TEN engine operations (every engine invocation is constructed Rust-side in `src/engine.rs` from a typed operation enum — the webview has NO shell permission of any kind and `tauri-plugin-shell` is not a dependency), B6 adding `engine_schedule_verify`, which is MUTATING: it re-issues the engine-side kickstart, so the live launchd job runs the engine; and Phase E (E12) adding `engine_update_check` — `update --check --json`, the Settings screen's "Check now" — which is NOT mutating (its one write is the engine's own update-check record), takes no operand, and leaves the request to the engine (one anonymous GET of the project's latest GitHub release); the webview itself still reaches no remote host. Then T11's three shell commands (`state_snapshot` reads the engine and derives the schedule state; `open_today` raises the window, for which the webview has no window permission at all; `app_quit` exits, and refuses until the Quit notice has been shown this session); B5's five: `read_latest_briefing` / `read_archived_briefing` READ the two engine files a briefing lives in (the archive command takes a validated calendar date, never a path; both join onto the paths `status --json` reports and never write), and `config_read` / `config_save` / `config_offer_notify_auto` are the app's ONE config-write path (JSON text in, never a path; `status --json`'s `paths.configPath`, never Tauri's config dir; engine-validated, atomic, `.bak` kept; `transcripts` and a literal API key cannot be changed); B6's four (T17): `access_snapshot` reports which macOS-protected folders this config reaches and what `doctor --json` says about them, `access_probe` READS ONE of four fixed protected folders from this process (a closed enum, never a path — it is the macOS prompt trigger and the revocation detector), `access_reveal_engine` reveals the managed engine copy whose path it re-reads from `schedule status --json`, and `access_open_settings` opens ONE of three fixed System Settings URLs chosen by a closed enum; and B7's two (T18): `notify_status` reads the app's notification opt-in record, the ENGINE's resolved `notify` value and the suppression log, and `notify_set_enabled` records the explained ask's answer — neither can post a notification. B8 adds four (T16 + dev 63): `config_create` is the FIRST-config path — the wizard's one write, JSON text in and never a path, engine-validated through `config validate --file`, EXCLUSIVELY created (anything already at the name — a file, a symlink, a racing `daily-briefing init` — is refused as `alreadyExists`, never replaced), with a literal `provider.api.apiKey` and any `transcripts` block refused outright; and the three `cli_shim_*` commands (the Settings screen's explicit "install command-line tool" action): `cli_shim_status` reads what sits at `/usr/local/bin/daily-briefing`, `cli_shim_install` writes a symlink there to the managed engine copy (target re-read from `schedule status --json`, never webview-supplied; a foreign file at the name is refused), and `cli_shim_remove` deletes only a symlink whose target is the managed copy or another name in the engine's state directory — none of the three takes an operand, and a permission refusal returns the exact manual command instead of escalating. B25 adds two (T25): `uninstall_preview` reads what an uninstall would remove (the app's own records, the window-state file, and — from `status --json` and `schedule status --json`, never the webview — the engine state dir's bounded list and the background scheduler's facts), and `uninstall_execute` performs it: FIRST the background scheduler, which it never unregisters itself (no `launchctl`, no `systemctl`) but hands to the engine's own `schedule uninstall --invoker app`, with `--take-over` only when its closed `schedule` operand says `removeAny` (`keep` calls nothing, and the default `removeOwn` refuses, without calling the engine, a scheduler this app did not install); then the app's OWN autostart entry via T19's plugin `disable()`, the app's OWN files, ONLY behind its first explicit boolean consent operand the engine-state entries, which mirror `scripts/uninstall.sh`'s `$SUPPORT`-rooted list token for token (set-equality with a test-time parse of the script, `tests/uninstall.rs`), plus on Linux the managed engine copy after its ownership checks, and ONLY behind its second the settings the engine's `configPath` folder holds (a key file a readable config names when it sits directly in that folder, `config.json`, `config.json.bak`, then the folder only if empty) — never a recursive delete of the support directory, and never a path from the webview. Phase E M5b adds two (T19 reworked): `autostart_set_enabled` turns the login item ON or OFF — the Settings toggle AND the setup wizard's last step — taking one boolean and nothing else (ON is the plugin's `enable()` followed, on macOS, by adding `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` = the bundle id to the plist it wrote; OFF is its `disable()`), and `autostart_wizard_default` READS the app's login-item record and the real state for the wizard's pre-tick; neither takes a path, and nothing at launch calls either. The LAST ONE is `tauri-plugin-autostart`'s `autostart:allow-is-enabled` (T19): the Settings toggle must reflect REAL state via `is_enabled()`, a stat of the plist, operand-free. The plugin's own `allow-enable` / `allow-disable` are NO LONGER granted (M5b): its `enable()` writes an unbranded plist, so every ON goes through `autostart_set_enabled` instead. NOTHING is granted for `tauri-plugin-notification` although it IS registered (the Rust-side post needs its managed state): its three live commands (`notify`, `request_permission`, `is_permission_granted`) are refused to the webview — posting is a Rust decision driven by the watcher, and `tests/capability.rs` pins the refusals as it does the tray's. NOTHING is granted for `tauri-plugin-window-state`: its persistence is entirely Rust-side. NOTHING is granted for `tauri-plugin-opener` either, and it is never registered on the builder, so its commands do not exist at runtime — `src/access.rs` calls its FREE functions Rust-side. The two caller-supplied operands (`run --json-out <name>`, `config validate --file <path>`) are validated in Rust before any spawn. This is deny-by-default only because `build.rs` declares an app ACL manifest — see the note there. capabilities/README.md carries the rationale, the B1 first-match-ceiling history this replaces, and the Known gaps.
